title: Revelations and records must reach Zion with a faithful companion
setting: Oliver Cowdery was assigned to carry the compiled revelations to Independence, Missouri, for printing. He was also to take money donated for the church there. On 11 November 1831, at Hiram, Ohio, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation. It sent John Whitmer, the church historian, with him. The two left for Missouri on 20 November. The Joseph Smith Papers editors call the date probable but not certain.
summary: The revelation says Oliver Cowdery should not travel alone with the commandments and the money. It names John Whitmer to go with him. Whitmer is to keep writing a history of important things about the church. He is to take counsel from Cowdery and others. Elders abroad are to send accounts of their stewardships to Zion. Zion is to be the place that receives these things. Whitmer is also to travel among the churches to gather knowledge and records. The work is for the generations who will grow up in Zion.

contextNote.title: A historian sent with the revelations
contextNote.text: The revelation first deals with safety: precious papers and money needed a trustworthy second traveler. Verse 2 chooses John Whitmer for that task. Verse 3 adds a lasting duty, to keep “writing and making a history” of the church. Verses 7–8 explain how he would gather it, by traveling and copying from church to church. Verse 8 also gives the purpose: the record is for “the rising generations” in Zion. In this passage, history means a gathered record meant to serve people not yet born.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 67–70 uses verse 1 to teach that “true and faithful” friends help us follow Jesus Christ. According to verses 3 and 8, what was John Whitmer, Oliver’s faithful companion, to record, and for whom?
reviewNote: Read all 8 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, 11 November 1831, Cowdery carrying the manuscript and money to Independence, and Whitmer as historian. JSP: Whitmer first wrote 11 October then corrected to November; a later history may imply 12 November, but editors prefer 11 November. JSP says the copy was probably made before they left on 20 November. Fact-check 2026-10-12: ldsText misdescribed the lesson; the CFM lesson uses 69:1 to teach that “true and faithful” friends help us follow Christ, and does not discuss record keeping under section 69.
